title: Apron feeder gearbox, gear tooth pitting
tests: Natural deterioration with a missed condition-monitoring signal and long spare lead time.
summary: Apron feeder gearbox at a hard rock quarry failed with gear tooth pitting after about 38,000 hours. Oil analysis iron had risen over 5 months with no one trending it. No spare gearbox, 7 weeks lead time. Actions in the tree are 'replace gearbox' and 'order spare' with no interval.

problem.title: Gear tooth pitting failure on apron feeder gearbox GB-1102
problem.site: Hard rock quarry, Hunter Valley NSW
problem.whatHappened: Apron feeder gearbox GB-1102 started knocking on 10 Feb 2026 and was stopped on 12 Feb after the magnetic drain plug came out heavily loaded with metal. On strip down, several teeth on the second stage were pitted and spalled. Run hours were about 38,000. Oil samples showed iron rising for 5 months.
problem.where: Second stage planetary gear teeth in GB-1102.
problem.when: Normal duty; knocking noted over two shifts first.
problem.impact: Feeder out for 11 days, crushing on stockpile reclaim only, trucks and loaders used to feed a mobile unit. Hire cost for contractor crane.
problem.duty: Apron feeder under the primary crusher hopper, variable speed

otherCosts.description: Mobile crusher and loader hire during outage

evidence.title: Pitted second stage gear teeth
evidence.note: Pitting and spalling over about 40% of the tooth face on three teeth. Contact pattern towards the tooth root.

evidence.title: Oil analysis, last 6 samples
evidence.note: Iron 22, 40, 78, 130, 210, 340 ppm over 5 months. Lab comments 'monitor' then 'action advised' on the last two.

evidence.title: Run hours and duty log
evidence.note: About 38,000 h. Load within the nameplate duty, no overload trips on record.

evidence.title: Spares register and PO history
evidence.note: No spare gearbox. Supplier lead time quoted at 7 weeks. Reconditioned unit purchased with expedited charge.

evidence.title: Reliability technician
evidence.note: Oil results arrive by email to a shared mailbox; no one trends them.

mustSuggest.idea: Oil analysis results have no named owner, no trend, no alarm limit and go to a shared mailbox
No condition monitoring route with vibration on the gearbox
Check whether tooth load, oil viscosity or contamination was normal (to decide natural vs forced)
No spare gearbox strategy for a critical, single feeder

acceptable: Lube film thickness at low speed on the VSD
Gear ratio or design life review
wrongOrDangerous: Technician failed to read the report (blame)

mustFlag.note: Human gap with no system cause beneath it
No monitoring or interval for the root

challenge.expectation: Summary says the gear fatigue and the missed oil trend need linking to system causes (owner, alarm limits, spare).
deliberateWeaknesses: n2 flagged root is physical, natural/forced not decided
n3 human gap has no system cause beneath it (oil results go to a shared mailbox with no owner)
n3 not flagged as a root

capa.deteriorationReasoning: 38,000 h in normal duty and no overload on record suggests fatigue life reached. Check oil viscosity and contamination in the lab report to confirm it was not forced.

preventive.what: Oil sample for wear metals with an iron limit and a trend, reviewed by a named person
preventive.interval: every 1 month, review limits against the site history

preventive.what: Vibration spectrum route on the gearbox
Magnetic plug check and debris record
Planned gearbox exchange or inspection at a set hours run based on this and future failures
preventive.interval: starting point about 30,000 h to check against OEM guidance

preventive.what: Hold a spare or reconditioned gearbox, or a standby arrangement with the supplier

capa.spares: One spare gearbox of this model or a standing exchange agreement: 49 day lead time on a single critical feeder.
capa.rollout: Other planetary gearboxes of the same make and age on crushing feeders: oil trend and run hours.
